page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance based on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor offering 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The instance includes 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction set features include AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and FMA flags. This instance lacks local disk storage and discrete GPUs, relying entirely on external block storage and providing a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates reliable multi-core throughput alongside lower single-core metrics. Single-threaded performance tests, such as stress-ng single-core (1312.39) and gzip compression (22.88 GB/sec), rank in the weaker bottom 25% percentile. Conversely, multi-threaded operations achieve average middle 50% benchmark results, recorded by a stress-ng multi-core score of 27992.16, a Geekbench multi-core score of 10181.0, and a bzip3 multi-threaded decompression rate of 127.99 GB/sec. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 109.69 GB/sec, while uncached write bandwidth is recorded at 47.96 GB/sec.

From a resource allocation standpoint, ecs.c6.8xlarge prioritizes vCPU density relative to memory, offering resource efficiency for workloads that do not require high per-core RAM capacity or bundled local storage. The key tradeoff is the lower single-core execution speed, which makes it less suited for unparallelized single-threaded processes. It is effective for parallel execution workloads, including multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving (achieving 20.38 GB/sec throughput), and in-memory key-value caching like Redis SET operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It features 16 physical cores, 32 dedicated vCPUs, and 64.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio suited for CPU-heavy tasks. The instance does not include integrated local SSD storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and offering a 10 Gbps network connection. Benchmark data highlights average multi-core performance, including a PassMark CPU score of 27240.11 and multi-core stress-ng score of 27992.16, alongside lower single-threaded processing speeds. Qualitative cost efficiency favors parallel computing scenarios where bundled local storage is unnecessary. Best-fit workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, containerized services, and database caching operations.
